- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent 5-day high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward moves at 10–15% below peak.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5–10% from recent peak within 5 days), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 1–2% per day.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 7–10 days); apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.6, -0.4, +0.8), model may misalign with sentiment; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
